ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word ends with the sound /v/? (1 mark)
   A. leave
   B. proof
   C. half
   D. leaf

2. Which of these is a reference material? (1 mark)
   A. A storybook
   B. A song
   C. A dictionary
   D. A letter

3. Which word is a definite article? (1 mark)
   A. some
   B. a
   C. the
   D. an

4. Which article goes before 'hour'? (1 mark)
   A. no article always
   B. the
   C. an
   D. a

5. Which plural is irregular? (1 mark)
   A. dishes
   B. boxes
   C. children
   D. books

6. What is the plural of 'potato'? (1 mark)
   A. potatoos
   B. potatoies
   C. potatoes
   D. potatos

7. Which word makes a request polite? (1 mark)
   A. please
   B. quick
   C. hurry
   D. now

8. Which is a negative sentence? (1 mark)
   A. I do not have enough money to buy a bicycle.
   B. Money is for buying.
   C. I have enough money.
   D. I bought a bicycle.

9. What does a foot bridge help people to do? (1 mark)
   A. Cross a road safely by walking over it
   B. Carry luggage
   C. Park cars
   D. Drive fast

10. Which pronoun replaces 'the children'? (1 mark)
   A. they
   B. it
   C. she
   D. he

11. Pronouns: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Ali and myself went to the clinic.
   B. Ali and I went to the clinic.
   C. Me and Ali went to the clinic.
   D. Ali and me went to the clinic.

12. Why should you use a mobile phone only with permission? (1 mark)
   A. Phones are only for adults to own
   B. It makes the battery last longer
   C. It makes calls cheaper
   D. It keeps you safe and responsible

13. A reading log helps you to (1 mark)
   A. hide your books
   B. remember what you have read
   C. break books
   D. sell books

14. Which material gives you news? (1 mark)
   A. A newspaper
   B. A dictionary
   C. A map key
   D. A story book

15. Which word means 'free time when you rest or play'? (1 mark)
   A. trust
   B. crime
   C. laptop
   D. leisure

16. Which word contains the sound /ɛə/? (1 mark)
   A. chest
   B. chair
   C. chin
   D. chop

17. What should you do before writing a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. Make a short plan
   B. Copy someone else's story
   C. Write the ending only
   D. Skip the beginning

18. Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   B. What did the barber put into his razor?
   C. What day did Baraka visit the barber?
   D. Where is the barbershop?

19. Which end mark is right for: 'How many books have you read'? (1 mark)
   A. .
   B. ?
   C. !
   D. ,

20. Which sentence is joined correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   B. We swept the floor, nor we wiped the desks.
   C. We swept the floor, yet we wiped the desks.
   D. We swept the floor, for we wiped the desks.

21. What is a topic sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A list of adjectives
   B. A sentence that tells what the paragraph is about
   C. The last word of the paragraph
   D. A question at the end

22. Which word means 'the leader of a team'? (1 mark)
   A. stadium
   B. captain
   C. whistle
   D. kit

23. Which word begins with the unvoiced sound /θ/? (1 mark)
   A. that
   B. the
   C. they
   D. thank

24. Which key words would help you find out how netball is played? (1 mark)
   A. password
   B. free prizes
   C. my address
   D. netball rules for children

25. Which question has the correct word order after 'where'? (1 mark)
   A. Where do you keep the ball?
   B. Where do you keeps the ball?
   C. Where you keep the ball?
   D. Where you do keep the ball?

26. Which is the best answer to 'Where is the stadium?' (1 mark)
   A. It is near the town.
   B. At three o'clock.
   C. The captain.
   D. Hers.

27. Which situation fits 'Little by little fills the measure'? (1 mark)
   A. Getting a big prize at once
   B. Picking up a little rubbish every day until the compound is clean
   C. Sleeping late
   D. Losing a shoe

28. Which sentence uses the correct participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. She has ate her lunch.
   B. She have eaten her lunch.
   C. She has eaten her lunch.
   D. She has eating her lunch.

29. Which is the negative of 'I have eaten'? (1 mark)
   A. I not have eaten.
   B. I has not eaten.
   C. I do not have eaten.
   D. I have not eaten.

30. What should you do if a website you find online worries you? (1 mark)
   A. Close it and tell a trusted adult
   B. Give your address
   C. Share it with everyone
   D. Ignore the adult

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does. (3 marks)

32. Use when, where, who and whose in four questions about a sports day. (4 marks)

33. Say whether the voice falls or rises at the end of: (a) Who sent the message? (b) Is the phone on the table? (2 marks)

34. Name three parts of a newspaper. (3 marks)

35. Write three yes/no questions about keeping the compound clean. (3 marks)

36. List the three parts of a narrative and say what each tells. (3 marks)

37. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a shop. Use one simile and two time words. (5 marks)

38. Name the three parts of fluent reading and explain each briefly. (3 marks)

39. List three places where we use a capital letter. (3 marks)

40. Write a short headline and two sentences for a news story about your school. (3 marks)

41. Write two ways you can show a speaker that you are listening actively. (2 marks)

42. Explain what 'prevention' means and use it in a sentence. (3 marks)

43. Explain what we learn from the story about honesty. (3 marks)

44. Replace the second mention with a pronoun: 'Neema saw the bridge. Neema liked the bridge.' (2 marks)

45. Read: 'Juma asked his mother to add vegetables to his lunch.' Say why Juma did this, using the story 'A Pot of Vegetables'. (2 marks)

46. Give three words with silent letters and name the silent letter in each. (3 marks)

47. Write one statement, one WH question and one yes or no question about email. Say how the voice moves in each. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — leave
   Leave ends with /v/. Leaf, half and proof end with /f/.

2. C — A dictionary
   A dictionary is used to look up spelling and meaning, so it is a reference book.

3. C — the
   The is the definite article.

4. C — an
   The h is silent, so hour starts with a vowel sound.

5. C — children
   Child becomes children, not childs.

6. C — potatoes
   Some nouns ending in o add es.

7. A — please
   Please turns an order into a polite request.

8. A — I do not have enough money to buy a bicycle.
   It says that the money is not sufficient.

9. A — Cross a road safely by walking over it
   It goes over the road.

10. A — they
   They stands for more than one.

11. B — Ali and I went to the clinic.
   I is the subject form.

12. D — It keeps you safe and responsible
   A trusted adult can guide you.

13. B — remember what you have read
   It records titles, dates and what you liked.

14. A — A newspaper
   Newspapers report news.

15. D — leisure
   Leisure is free time.

16. B — chair
   'Chair' ends with the /ɛə/ sound.

17. A — Make a short plan
   A plan helps organise beginning, middle and end.

18. A — How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   You work out his feelings from clues.

19. B — ?
   It is a direct question.

20. A — We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   'And' adds an idea.

21. B — A sentence that tells what the paragraph is about
   It states the main idea.

22. B — captain
   The captain leads the team.

23. D — thank
   'Thank' has the unvoiced 'th'.

24. D — netball rules for children
   Good key words describe the topic you want.

25. A — Where do you keep the ball?
   The helping verb 'do' comes before the subject.

26. A — It is near the town.
   'Where' asks for a place.

27. B — Picking up a little rubbish every day until the compound is clean
   Small efforts add up.

28. C — She has eaten her lunch.
   Has + eaten.

29. D — I have not eaten.
   Add not after have.

30. A — Close it and tell a trusted adult
   Staying safe means asking for help.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part with its job.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: When is sports day? Where is it held? Who is the guest of honour? Whose team is winning?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) falls (b) rises
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Masthead (name), headline, byline, article, picture, caption, advert, weather report (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Do you sweep the compound? Is the bin covered? Can we plant a tree?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events. End: how it finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words with beginning, middle and end, one simile, two time words such as first and then, and correct punctuation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, events, simile, time words, and punctuation.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accuracy: reading the words correctly. Speed: reading at a comfortable, not rushed pace. Expression: using the voice to show meaning and feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part explained.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people; names of places; days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Headline: Pupils Win Football Match. The school team won 2 to 1 on Friday. The pupils were happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a headline and 1 for each sentence.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and nod; keep still and quiet; say 'I see'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prevention means acting so that something bad does not happen. For example: Washing hands is a way of prevention.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the meaning, 1 for a sentence.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema saw the bridge. She liked it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for she and 1 mark for it.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama Zuri told him vegetables give vitamins that protect the body from sickness, so he wanted to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for vitamins or protection and 1 mark for linking to Juma.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: knee (k), debt (b), honest (h).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with its silent letter.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: I sent the email (falls). Where is the message? (falls) Did you get it? (rises)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with correct voice movement.
